target_customer: Consumers who read articles, newsletters and long form web content and pay for a premium reading app
problem: Read it later tools such as Instapaper and Pocket had lagged behind how people read online today, with no good way to save media, collect newsletters, highlight and share what you read.
business_model: Consumer freemium subscription (free app, paid premium tiers)
product_category: Consumer read it later and reading app

founders.name: Ben Springwater
founders.background_notes: Met co-founder while working at Nextdoor per TechCrunch. Education not found.

founders.name: Robert Mackenzie
founders.background_notes: Met co-founder while working at Nextdoor per TechCrunch. Education not found.

competitors.name: Instapaper
competitors.what: Read it later app founded by Marco Arment, majority stake sold to Betaworks in 2013
competitors.traction_then: established product with a long user base, no figures found
competitors.funding_then: owned by Betaworks per search snippet of Wikipedia

competitors.name: Pocket
competitors.what: Read it later service that began as a Firefox extension in 2007, acquired by Mozilla in 2017
competitors.funding_then: owned by Mozilla since 2017 per Wikipedia reference

technical_complexity.rationale: A consumer reading app with web and iOS clients, article parsing, newsletter ingestion and text to speech. Standard engineering for a small team with no research risk.

defensibility.rationale: A saved library and highlights create some lock in, but incumbents Pocket and Instapaper and later Readwise Reader offered nearly the same features and exports are easy.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Pocket was shut down by Mozilla in 2025 per a 2026 TechCrunch alternatives roundup, which pushed users toward apps like Matter. Readwise Reader remains a named main competitor.

market_need_then: TechCrunch in 2021 described first generation read it later apps as having lagged behind how people read online, and a GV partner said he was a heavy user of them. Newsletters had grown strongly in 2020.

branding.domain_note: Launched on getmatter.app and later moved to getmatter.com; date of the move not found.

identity.logo: Not described by an opened source
identity.visual_style: Reading as something almost enchanting, per the company page
identity.voice_and_tone: Literary, quotes Ursula K. Le Guin 'Words are my matter' on the company page

branding.brand_signature: Ursula K. Le Guin quote on the company page
branding.community_and_virality: Several app review sites and blogs wrote about it as a read later alternative, including MacStories and The Sweet Setup per search results; contents not opened.

brand_strength.rationale: Generic common word shared by many unrelated brands, so name searches return other companies. The company page voice is distinctive but little press about the brand itself was found.

outcome_analysis: Matter went from an angel round to a YC slot in summer 2020, a $2 million seed, and a $7 million Series A led by GV in October 2021, on the thesis that Pocket and Instapaper had stagnated. It is still active as of 2026 with app updates, though a third party tracker estimates small usage and revenue. Pocket's 2025 shutdown boosted interest in alternatives but also brought Readwise Reader into focus as the main rival.
notes: Seed date not stated by TechCrunch; an aggregator snippet gave a 125K seed dated 2020-08, unverified and different from the 2 million figure. TechCrunch says the founders began building in early 2020 after an angel round of unknown size. The founders said they had raised about 9 million total at the Series A, consistent with the sum. Competitor sources predate the batch; no 2020 dated source was found. Search for acquisition or shutdown found none; usage estimates from a tracker are unverified. Brand name origin not found; a search for the name returned unrelated Matter brands.
